headline: US DFC BACKS GLOBAL ATOMIC'S DASA WITH $414M — AFRICA'S HIGHEST-GRADE URANIUM DEPOSIT CLEARED FOR FINANCING
snippet: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation approved a debt facility of up to US$414 million for Global Atomic's Dasa uranium project in Niger — Africa's highest-grade uranium deposit — two years after Washington's troops were expelled from the country; conditions include finding a viable yellowcake export route and extending the mining convention, but the deal represents the largest US strategic investment in African uranium in decades and validates the company's $250 million already committed to the project.

headline: PAN GLOBAL DRILLS 83M AT 1.74 G/T GOLD IN SPAIN — CÁRMENES NEW ZONE PEAKS AT 32.2 G/T FROM 9M DEPTH
snippet: Pan Global Resources drilled 83 metres at 1.74 g/t gold from just 9 metres depth at the Providencia target within its Cármenes Project in northern Spain, with a peak of 32.2 g/t over 0.5 metres — dramatically expanding confidence in a new gold zone within a project that already carries a significant polymetallic resource; the near-surface intercept starts a new chapter for a property previously defined primarily by copper and silver.

headline: NEWCORE GOLD HITS 69M AT 2.59 G/T IN GHANA — 6.41 G/T OVER 24M IS WIDEST HIGH-GRADE ZONE AT ENCHI
snippet: Newcore Gold intersected 2.59 g/t Au over 69 metres — including 6.41 g/t Au over 24 metres from 59 metres — at the Boin target within its 80,000-metre Enchi Gold Project in Ghana, representing one of the widest and highest grade-thickness intercepts encountered in the program to date and confirming significant bulk-mineable potential at the margin of the main resource envelope.

headline: WAR DEPT. COMMITS $450M TO SECURE US TUNGSTEN CHAIN — GOLDHAVEN'S B.C. PROJECT IN THE SPOTLIGHT
snippet: The U.S. Department of War committed $450 million on September 14 to The Elmet Group to rebuild domestic tungsten manufacturing and international mining supply — allocating $165 million to US plants in Maine, Michigan, and Ohio, and funding mining in Australia and Spain; Canadian junior GoldHaven Resources (CSE) highlighted the announcement alongside its active drilling at the Kuhn tungsten system in northern British Columbia, positioning itself as a potential supply-chain beneficiary.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD HITS VISIBLE GOLD IN FIRST DRILL AT MUD LAKE NORTH — NEW ONTARIO TARGET 3KM FROM GOLD ROCK
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSXV: DRY) reported visible gold in the third drill hole of its maiden program at Mud Lake North — approximately 3 kilometres north of its Gold Rock target in Ontario — with broad alteration and sulphide zones confirmed in the first two holes before visible gold appeared; assays are pending for all three holes in the first-ever drilling of this target within the Gold Rock Camp, with 2,000 metres planned to test down-plunge and strike extensions.

headline: PUREPOINT HITS 7.4M AT 8,760 CPS AT NEW Q24 TARGET — ATHABASCA DISCOVERY GROWING BEYOND NOVA ZONE
snippet: Purepoint Uranium (TSXV: PTU) intersected 7.4 metres averaging 8,760 counts per second at the unconformity — including 0.5 metres at 38,710 CPS — in the first hole at the new Q24 target within the Dorado Joint Venture in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin; the radioactive interval occurs within strongly altered basement rocks at a third distinct target area separate from both Nova and Q23, suggesting the Dorado mineralizing system may be materially broader than initially mapped, with lab assays from all summer holes still pending.

headline: GOLD TERRA ADDS TWO RIGS AT CON MINE — 3-RIG FALL DRILL TARGETS MRE GROWTH AHEAD OF PEA, YELLOWKNIFE
snippet: Gold Terra Resource (TSXV: YGT) expanded its 2026 fall drill program at the Con Mine Option Property in Yellowknife, NWT to three rigs, adding the Yellorex zone and historical tailings storage facility as targets with sonic drilling aimed at adding ounces to the June 2026 initial MRE ahead of a Preliminary Economic Assessment; the company's Newmont option remains valid until November 2027, giving a defined window to prove out the deposit.

headline: COPPER SLIPS AS ANDES SUPPLY PIPELINE STALLS — CHILE AND PERU PERMITTING DELAYS SHADOW NEAR-RECORD PRICES
snippet: Copper retreated on September 17 as market focus shifted to structural supply constraints from Chile and Peru — the two largest producers — where permitting delays and cost inflation are slowing new mine development at precisely the moment demand-side analysts argue the market needs incremental tonnes; the pullback came from just below the all-time LME high of $14,875/tonne reached last week, with backwardation in the term structure signalling physical tightness remains intact.

headline: INDONESIA SLASHES NICKEL ORE PRICE FORMULA — BATTERY SUPPLY CHAIN COST RELIEF EFFECTIVE SEPT 15
snippet: Indonesia's Energy Ministry cut the corrective factor for low-grade nickel ore (1.2% Ni) to 14% from 26% and reduced the cobalt factor to 17% from 30%, effective September 15, 2026 — lowering input costs for the world's largest nickel-producing nation and providing what domestic smelters called long-awaited operational certainty as they compete against Chinese processors for EV battery material contracts.

headline: SPROTT URANIUM WATCH: INVESTORS ACTING WITH CONVICTION AS SPOT HITS $82 — JUNIORS UP 21.75% IN SEPTEMBER
snippet: Sprott's September 2026 uranium market analysis notes spot uranium rebounding to $82 per pound — up 8% from August lows — with the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index up 17% and juniors up 21.75% month-to-date, driven by structural supply cuts: Cameco slashing McArthur River guidance and Kazatomprom lowering 2026 production, while the World Nuclear Association projects reactor requirements to more than double by 2040 on SMR and new entrant demand; Sprott observes institutional investors rotating into uranium with conviction not seen since 2023.
